transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because my eating has been a little hard to manage lately. It’s not every day, but some evenings after work—especially if I’ve been really “good” or strict with myself all day—I end up eating much more than I planned. Like I’ll have dinner, and then somehow it turns into cereal, crackers, leftovers, maybe something sweet… all within a couple hours. I know that probably doesn’t sound great, but I’m not sure how concerned I should be.
Can you describe how you feel while you're eating all of that after work? Do you feel like you can stop if you wanted to, or does it feel like you're not in control?

I mean… I’d like to say I could stop, and sometimes I tell myself, “Okay, that’s enough,” but on those nights it doesn’t really feel that simple. Once I get started, I keep going back to the kitchen even while I’m kind of telling myself not to. I don’t really feel like I’m back in charge until I’m already uncomfortably full… if that makes sense.
Do these episodes bother you or interfere with your daily life in any way, like affecting your mood, work, or relationships?

It bothers me some, yeah… though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything. I’m still keeping up with my clients at work, and I do some mentoring there too, and things at home are getting done.

But I guess it does get in my head. Like before public events or meetings, if I’m worried about how my clothes fit, I can feel distracted and not as confident as I normally would. I don’t know if that counts as interfering, but it’s uncomfortable.
After these episodes of eating more than you plan, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or do extra exercise to try to control your weight or how your body looks?

Um… I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that. And I don’t use laxatives.

I guess… the thing I do is more like trying to “balance it out” the next day. Like if I had one of those nights, I’ll tell myself I’m making up for it by skipping breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take a really long hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m tired. I don’t know if that’s the same kind of thing you mean, but… yeah, I do that sometimes.
Do you ever skip meals or exercise a lot to compensate for eating normally, or is it only after those evenings when you eat more than you planned?

It’s mostly after those evenings, I think. Like… I don’t usually skip meals just for no reason or after a regular dinner.

But if I had one of those nights where I ate more than I meant to, the next day I’ll kind of tell myself I’m just getting back on track. So I might skip breakfast and lunch, or take an extra-long hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m already tired. I know that probably sounds a little… I don’t know. I try to make it seem like it’s just being disciplined, but it’s usually tied to making up for the night before.
Do you ever feel upset, guilty, or ashamed specifically about the ways you try to balance things out, like skipping meals or exercising a lot after those evenings of eating more than planned?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just being responsible or getting back on track, so I don’t feel as bad about it.

But honestly, the next day after one of those nights, when I’m skipping breakfast and lunch or making myself take a really long hike, or pushing harder at softball even when I’m tired… I do feel kind of embarrassed about it. Like I know I’m “making up for it,” even if I don’t want to call it that. I don’t love admitting that.

Can you tell me more about the feeling you have while you're eating during these episodes—does it ever feel like you're not really in control, like you're on autopilot or can't stop even if you wanted to?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but sometimes it does feel that way.

Once I get started on those nights, it’s like I keep going back into the kitchen even while part of me is saying, “Okay, stop now.” And I’ll tell myself I’m done, but then I’m back getting something else. I don’t really feel like I’m back in charge until I’m already uncomfortably full.

I know that probably sounds bad… but that’s the honest answer.
Can you describe if, during these episodes, you feel like you're not in control of your eating, like you can't stop even if you want to?

Yeah… I think I already kind of said this, but yes, that’s probably the part that bothers me most.

It’s not like I plan to keep eating like that. I’ll tell myself, okay, that’s enough, stop now. But then I’ll find myself going back into the kitchen again anyway. It feels like I’m not really fully in control until I’m already too full and uncomfortable.

I don’t know if that makes sense, but… yeah, that’s how it feels.
Do you ever feel really upset, frustrated, or distressed specifically while you’re eating during these episodes — like you wish you could stop but can’t, or that you’re losing control?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m being dramatic, but yes, I do get upset with myself while it’s happening.

It’s like once I get started, I keep going back to the kitchen even though I’m telling myself, “Just stop, that’s enough.” And I don’t really feel like I’m back in control until I’m already uncomfortably full. It’s frustrating… and kind of embarrassing to admit, honestly.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're completely unable to stop eating, even if part of you wants to?

Yeah… I guess “completely unable” sounds so strong, but it does feel close to that in the moment.

Once I start on those nights, I keep ending up back in the kitchen even while I’m telling myself, “Stop, you’ve had enough.” And I don’t really feel like I’m back in charge until I’m already uncomfortably full.

I know I’ve kind of said that already, but… yes, that’s what it feels like.
How often do these episodes happen, and does the frequency of them bother you or cause you significant distress?

It’s not every day or anything… but for the past few months, it’s been most weeks, I think. Usually maybe one or two nights in a week where I eat way more than I meant to.

And… yes, it does bother me. I try not to make a huge deal out of it, but the next day I usually feel like I need to fix it somehow, so I’ll skip meals or exercise longer than I normally would. I know that probably doesn’t sound great… but that’s what’s been happening.
Do you feel a lot of distress or emotional discomfort specifically about your eating habits, like feeling out of control or upset about what you're doing?

Yes… I do. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s not that big of a deal, but it feels pretty awful when it’s happening.

Once I get started on those nights, I keep going back to the kitchen even though I’m telling myself to stop. And I don’t really feel like I’m back in charge until I’m already uncomfortably full. So… yes, I guess that is a lot of distress about it.
Do you feel that your judgment of yourself is strongly influenced by your body shape or weight, like how you see yourself affects how you feel about your worth as a person?

I wouldn’t want to say my whole worth depends on it… that sounds kind of dramatic. But, yes, it affects me more than I like to admit.

Like if I’m getting ready for a client luncheon or a leadership meeting and my waistband feels tight, I immediately start thinking I look sloppy, or like people aren’t going to take me as seriously. Even though I know I’m still doing my job and nothing has really changed.

I know that probably sounds a little vain, but it’s more like… I just feel less put together as a person when my body feels wrong.
Do you judge yourself in a harsh or critical way based on your body shape or weight, even if others might not notice anything different?

Yes… I think I do, probably more than I should.

It’s not like other people would necessarily notice anything, but if my waistband feels tight before a client luncheon or a leadership meeting, I start feeling like I look sloppy. Then I worry people won’t take me as seriously, even though I know I’m still doing my job the same way.

I know that may sound silly, but in the moment I’m pretty hard on myself about it.
